report.analysis.baseline_note: delta_*_pct is the change of the current run against the baseline, in percent.
report.analysis.drift: Within {step}: the value changed by {change} % from the start to the end of the step at a constant load.

report.analysis.step_table_note: RPS is the step level. Response time is the p95 on the plateau, without the tail after a drop.
report.analysis.timeline_note: Values are plateau means of each step, without the dip and the load decline after the plateau (those are in step_table.per_step.after_plateau). The load level of a step is steps[].rps_level. Row order: load testing tool metrics first, then the metrics with the largest relative change.

report.findings.title: Problems and recommendations
report.focus.soak: Check that the target load is held over the whole run without accumulating degradation.
report.focus.spike: Check the reaction to a sharp load increase: latency and error growth in the spike window and the recovery time.
report.focus.step: Find the maximum sustainable throughput and the moment degradation starts.
report.focus.stress: Find the saturation point, the degradation pattern and the limiting resource.
report.hero.no_final: The final report for this run is not ready yet. If it is being generated, reload the page later; the job status is shown in the archive.
report.hero.unverified.one: {n} finding is not confirmed by data and is not counted in the verdict rationale.
report.hero.unverified.other: {n} findings are not confirmed by data and are not counted in the verdict rationale.
report.hero.unverified_no_revision.one: {n} finding is not confirmed by data and is not counted in the verdict rationale (the model's verification pass did not run).
report.hero.unverified_no_revision.other: {n} findings are not confirmed by data and are not counted in the verdict rationale (the model's verification pass did not run).
report.hold_note.early_drop: RPS dropped long before the end of the test: the drop is inside the hold window
report.hold_note.long_ramp_up: the ramp-up took more than half of the test: the hold window is the whole test
report.hold_note.no_steady_level: RPS never held a steady level: the hold window is the whole test
report.invalid.hint: Check the token limit and the prompt, then generate again.
report.invalid.not_valid: The model's answer looks like JSON but failed validation, so it is not shown as a full report.
report.invalid.title: LLM response structure error
report.judge.criteria_title: What the score is based on
report.judge.data.label_grounding: Direct references to metric and series names: {pct}
report.judge.data.numeric: Numbers in the text that match: {pct} ({supported} of {total} confirmed)
report.judge.data.numeric_none: Numbers in the text that match: not checked, the findings have no explicit numeric claims.
report.judge.data_fair: The data check mostly supports the conclusions.
report.judge.data_good: The data check supports the conclusions well.
report.judge.data_weak: The data check supports the conclusions weakly: verify them against the charts.
report.judge.footer: The data check is heuristic: it rates how the text is tied to the metrics, whether the numbers match and whether peak_performance is consistent; it does not fact-check every sentence.
report.judge.intro_skipped: The model gave a single answer, so the judge did not run: there was nothing to choose from.
report.judge.intro_unavailable: The judge gave no score: {reason}. The result is based on the data check and the model's confidence.
report.judge.judge_skipped: Judge: did not run, the model gave a single answer
report.judge.notes.context_truncated: For this report the judge worked with a shortened context.
report.judge.notes.safe_path: This answer was scored in the compatible fallback mode without the domain rubric.
report.judge.notes.truncated_candidates: Some candidate answers in this report were shortened before scoring: {count}.
report.judge.reason_error: the model call failed, see the application log for details
report.judge.reason_partial: it did not score every answer option
report.judge.reason_unparsed: its answer could not be parsed
report.judge.rubric.sla_alignment: Account of the SLA and risks: {pct}
report.judge.subtitle_default: how the AI answer was chosen and checked
report.judge.subtitle_skipped: by the data check, without the judge
report.judge.subtitle_unavailable: by the data check: the judge gave no score
report.judge.summary.binding_weak: The judge rates the answer highly, but the text is loosely tied to specific metrics and series from the context.
report.judge.summary.both_reserved: Both the judge and the heuristic data check give the answer modest scores.
report.judge.summary.close: The judge and the heuristic data check give similar scores.
report.judge.summary.data_better: The data supports the answer better than the judge's score suggests: it probably lacked completeness or specifics.
report.judge.summary.data_partial: The judge rates the answer highly, but the heuristic data check confirms it only partly.
report.judge.summary.final_lower: The final score is noticeably lower than the judge's because the data check found little support.
report.judge.summary.labels_weak: The numbers in the text mostly match the data, but the findings rarely name metrics and series from the context directly.
report.judge.summary.labels_weak_peak: The numbers in the text mostly match the data, but the findings rarely name metrics and series directly, and peak_performance was not confirmed.
report.judge.summary.numbers_weak: The judge rates the answer highly, but the data weakly supports the numeric claims in the text.
report.judge.summary.peak_mismatch: The main conclusions are partly confirmed, but the peak_performance value differs noticeably from the value computed from the data.
report.judge.summary.reliable: The answer looks reliable: both the judge and the heuristic data check rate it highly.
report.judge.summary.service: This is an internal score of the answer quality: it helps pick the best candidate among several answers.
